goals: mechanistic: characterize deep drainage/recharge flux (water that would transport nitrate) beneath fertilized vs non-fertilized land on contrasting soils
validation: compare predicted well nitrate arrival concentrations to external well nitrate records (NOT achievable with this stack — see feasibility)
key_processes: reactive nitrate transport in the saturated zone (NOT represented)
lateral groundwater flow along field-to-well paths (NOT represented)
well capture-zone travel time and mixing (NOT represented)

model_choice.rationale: ELM can resolve vadose-zone recharge/drainage as a loading-potential proxy, but the requested quantity (nitrate arrival concentration at wells) is a saturated-zone reactive-transport result outside the single-column stack.
model_choice.coupling_note: Answering the question as posed requires ELM recharge + a nitrogen-leaching source term to drive a PFLOTRAN reactive-transport model toward well capture zones. This coupler, the reactive N chemistry, and the flow-path geometry are all unbuilt — listed in requires_capabilities.

answerable: seasonal magnitude and timing of deep drainage/recharge (QDRAI/QCHARGE) beneath fertilized row-crop vs non-crop land
soil-drainage-class control on that recharge flux (SSURGO-driven)
relative ranking of land-use x soil combinations by leaching-water potential (a proxy, not a concentration)

not_answerable.aspect: nitrate arrival concentration at drinking-water wells
not_answerable.why: single-column ELM carries no leachable nitrate tracer and has no lateral/saturated groundwater transport, so there is no field-to-well flow path or arrival concentration
not_answerable.needs: ELM->PFLOTRAN reactive-transport coupling with a nitrate species

not_answerable.why: columns are independent 1-D points with no lateral flow or routing
not_answerable.needs: saturated-zone lateral flow + well capture-zone geometry

not_answerable.why: ELM land-use lever changes vegetation/ET, not an applied-fertilizer nitrate export concentration in drainage

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (land use x soil drainage class) — screening design for recharge/loading potential only
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 land-use classes x 2 soil drainage classes = 6 cells; +2 light replicates in the dominant fertilized-row-crop x well-drained combination (the highest leaching-potential and most policy-relevant cell). Small N is appropriate because this is only a proxy screening of recharge — the actual transport question is not answerable here, so a dense grid would over-claim.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: concentrate columns in intensively fertilized row-crop areas on well-drained soils (highest recharge + highest nitrate loading potential) and in near-stream / high-recharge positions; contrast against poorly-drained and non-crop cells. Elevation is NOT a stratification axis (160 m relief; not the mechanism).
sampling_strategy.replication: 2 extra columns in fertilized-row-crop x well-drained to gauge within-stratum soil variability for the highest-risk class

sampling_plan.reason: highest recharge + highest nitrate-loading potential; the primary leaching-risk cell (includes 2 replicates for within-stratum variability)
row-crop loading but suppressed vertical recharge; contrasts drainage-class control on leaching water
isolates land-use effect on recharge at fixed favorable drainage
background recharge with minimal N input, well-drained

validation_design.comparison: none — qualitative comparison to literature recharge ranges only
NOT POSSIBLE — ELM produces no nitrate concentration and no field-to-well flow path; well records cannot validate any ELM output. Recorded as a gap, not a comparison.
validation_design.n_validation_points: 0 (usable) — records exist but are unmatchable to model output without reactive-transport coupling

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: baseline NLDAS-2 forcing, native SSURGO soil per column, WTD-informed warm start; recharge screening only (not nitrate transport)

requires_capabilities.capability: ELM->PFLOTRAN reactive-transport coupling with a nitrate species
requires_capabilities.why: the question is a saturated-zone reactive solute-transport problem; ELM recharge must drive PFLOTRAN reactive transport
fertilizer input to leached-nitrate concentration in drainage is not an ELM output
requires_capabilities.blocks: the nitrate loading flux entering transport

requires_capabilities.capability: saturated-zone lateral groundwater flow + well capture-zone geometry
requires_capabilities.why: single-column ELM has no lateral flow or field-to-well travel path
requires_capabilities.blocks: travel time, mixing, and arrival timing

requires_capabilities.why: to connect distributed field recharge to specific well capture zones
requires_capabilities.blocks: spatial attribution of loading to wells

requires_capabilities.why: to place and parameterize fertilized-field strata
to define receptors and enable any future validation

requires_capabilities.capability: model spin-up (already supported) applied to recharge target
requires_capabilities.why: recharge/water-table states require spin-up or WTD warm start to be meaningful

assumptions: Upper Iowa is within CONUS, so NLDAS-2 12 km forcing applies.
SSURGO soil and a land-use/crop raster are resolvable in-domain for the downstream expander.
The 'well nitrate records (external)' are point concentration measurements with locations, not recharge or flux observations.
Elevation relief (~160 m) is not a controlling driver here and is intentionally not a stratification axis.
The recharge screening is a loading-potential proxy only and does not represent nitrate attenuation, denitrification in the saturated zone, or mixing.
open_questions: Is the goal a defensible nitrate arrival concentration (needs the full coupled reactive-transport stack), or an interim ranking of recharge/leaching-potential hotspots (achievable now)?
Are fertilizer application rates/timing and crop rotation data available for the source-term model?
Are well locations, depths, and screen intervals available to define capture zones for a future PFLOTRAN coupling?
Is there any recharge or vadose-zone flux observation to validate the ELM recharge proxy, or is validation entirely dependent on the unbuilt transport chain?
